name: How do you choose a multi-family contractor for a tight urban site?

mainEntity.name: What should you look for in a contractor for a multi-family project on a cramped city lot?
mainEntity.text: What should you look for in a contractor for a multi-family project on a cramped city lot?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a cramped urban site, the contractor’s experience matters as much as price. The right team should have a record of building multi-family projects with limited access, difficult staging, and frequent inspections. Ask how they handle deliveries, crane or pump placement, pedestrian protection, neighbor communication, and trade sequencing. A good contractor should also be comfortable working with city reviewers and resolving field issues quickly. The lowest bid can become the most expensive choice if the team has not managed dense-site logistics before. Owners should look for detailed preconstruction planning, realistic schedules, and transparent change-order practices. References from similar urban apartment projects are more valuable than general residential experience because the risks are very different.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose a contractor with proven experience on tight urban sites, permit-heavy projects, and occupied neighborhoods. The right team should show clear scheduling, logistics planning, safety control, and strong communication with inspectors and neighbors. On small city lots, experience with access, staging, and sequencing matters more than low bid alone.
